title: Is Japan’s Repatriation Wave Starting?
gist: Gavekal argues rising JGB yields have begun shifting Japanese investors' calculus on their ~US$5trn of overseas assets, with a net ¥5.5trn of foreign portfolio assets repatriated in the 12 months to September 2026. The Bank of Japan's late-October stance shift could accelerate this incipient flow, creating a structural bid for the deeply undervalued yen.

insights.claim: Japanese portfolio investors hold roughly US$5trn in overseas assets, and the key open question for global markets is when the risks of holding them will outweigh the relative rewards and trigger large-scale repatriation.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: A sustained Japanese repatriation is a tail risk for global asset prices given the size of the overseas holdings.

insights.so_what: Higher JGB yields reduce the incentive to hold foreign assets; further JGB yield rises strengthen the repatriation case.
